candidates.requirement: Initialize every mode byte examined by gzopen.
candidates.target_route: Input bytes [14, 119] make mode_sz 14, copy 'w' into mode[0], leave mode[1] through mode[12] uninitialized, and place the terminator at mode[13].
candidates.failure_condition: gz_open examines mode bytes after 'w' while interpreting the mode, so this target execution reads an uninitialized byte.
candidates.alternative_paths: The entry calls gzopen before its operation switch; no other route avoids this read for the witness.

candidates.requirement: Initialize all size × nitems bytes passed to gzfwrite.
candidates.target_route: Input bytes [0, 119, 1, 2] open with mode 'w'. The first operation calls gzbuffer with size 1; the second selects gzfwrite with default size and item count 8, leaving 63 of its 64 input bytes uninitialized.
candidates.failure_condition: gzfwrite requests all 64 bytes and gz_write passes that buffer to compression.
candidates.alternative_paths: The selected switch arm has one gzfwrite call. Its default counts remain 8 when the witness has no remaining bytes; cleanup cannot undo the read.

candidates.requirement: Keep a write-mode gzFile available for a compatible close call.
candidates.target_route: Input bytes [0, 119, 1, 21] open in write mode, call gzbuffer, then select gzclose_r.
candidates.failure_condition: gzclose_r rejects a write-mode file without freeing it. The harness nevertheless sets file to NULL, so exit cleanup cannot close or free that file.
candidates.alternative_paths: The only later close receives NULL; remove(fname) does not close the retained descriptor or free the gzFile.

candidates.requirement: Select a whence element within the whences array before calling gzseek.
candidates.target_route: Input bytes [0, 119, 1, 4, 5] open in write mode, call gzbuffer, then select gzseek with an index of 5.
candidates.failure_condition: The array has five elements, while the selector uses modulo 6; index 5 reads beyond the array before gzseek can validate whence.
candidates.alternative_paths: The selected switch arm computes whence once. Other input values can select valid elements, but provide no alternative route for this execution.
